**1 — Scene:** A breakfast-style meal: several strips of bacon alongside browned shredded potatoes topped with a tomato-onion mixture.

**2 — Vessel:** A round dinner plate, estimated at **26 cm diameter**. Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Bacon; fried shredded potatoes/hash browns; chopped tomato, onion and green herbs or peppers, resembling salsa. Cooking fat is included in the cooked-food energy estimates rather than counted separately.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:** Areas are allocated without double-counting overlapping toppings.

| Item | Plate area | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bacon strips | 23% | 122 cm² × 0.5 cm = 61 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 55 g | 500 | 275 kcal |
| Fried shredded potatoes | 32% | 170 cm² × 2 cm = 340 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 221 g | 190 | 420 kcal |
| Tomato-onion salsa | 10% | 53 cm² × 1 cm = 53 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 34 g | 30 | 10 kcal |

The allocated areas total **65% of the plate**, consistent with the substantial exposed rim and upper-right area.

**8 — Sanity check:** About **310 g and 705 kcal** is plausible for the visible potato mound and several bacon strips. The main uncertainties are bacon thickness and the amount of fat used to fry the potatoes.
